summary: Since 15 September 2026 Thailand grants visa-free entry of up to 30 days for tourism to passport holders of 60 countries and territories, with other stays for a few nationalities under bilateral agreements, and a visa on arrival for Azerbaijani, Belarusian and Serbian citizens; everyone else applies through a single global eVisa portal, and all foreign arrivals must submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) before travel.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. WHO's country list gives the requirement for travellers aged 9 months or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission, and for travellers who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of such a country.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read requires travel insurance of visa-exempt visitors or tourist-visa holders. The Royal Thai Embassy in Washington says certain visas (Non-Immigrant O-A and O-X) require a Foreign Insurance Certificate.

onwardTicket.text: The UK Foreign Office says you may be asked to show evidence of onward or return travel, and that British nationals have been refused entry for failing to provide it.

proofOfFunds.text: You may be asked to show adequate funds. The Royal Thai Embassy in Washington says travellers entering under the Tourist Visa Exemption Scheme must have at least 20,000 THB per person (40,000 THB per family). Under the Ministry of Interior announcement, as listed by the Tourism Authority of Thailand, the amounts are 10,000 THB per person (20,000 THB per family) on a visa on arrival or a transit visa, and 20,000 THB per person (40,000 THB per family) on a tourist or non-immigrant visa. Children under 12 are exempt.

declarations.text: All foreign nationals arriving in Thailand must submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card online before entry. The Immigration Bureau's website for it is tdac.immigration.go.th.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to take more than 200 cigarettes per person into Thailand; excess cigarettes are likely to be confiscated and you could be fined 10 times their value.

The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to possess or use any vape, e-cigarette, pod, e-liquid or heat-not-burn device in Thailand, with no exceptions for tourists; offences can lead to confiscation, heavy fines, detention and court proceedings.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises guarding against pickpocketing and bag-snatchers, especially on motorbikes. It advises against all but essential travel to parts of the far south near the Malaysian border and to areas within 20 km of the land border with Cambodia.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says overstaying costs 500 baht a day, up to 20,000 baht, and that you risk detention, deportation at your own expense and a re-entry ban of up to 10 years.
Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal to possess or use in Thailand — the UK Foreign Office says there are no exceptions for tourists or for personal use.

The UK Foreign Office says criticising the Thai monarchy (lèse-majesté) is illegal, that the law can be interpreted broadly and carries a long prison sentence, and that people have been charged over comments and shared articles online.
The Immigration Bureau says foreigners submit the TDAC on its website, tdac.immigration.go.th.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Thailand?
faq.answer: No. Since 15 September 2026, US passport holders can enter Thailand visa-free for up to 30 days for tourism. They must still submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) before arrival.

faq.question: What is the TDAC and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Thailand Digital Arrival Card is an online arrival form that every foreign national must submit within 3 days before arriving in Thailand, at tdac.immigration.go.th. It replaced the paper arrival card.

faq.question: How much does a Thailand tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: For nationalities that need one, the single-entry tourist visa costs USD 40 and the 6-month multiple-entry visa (METV) USD 200 when applied for through the Royal Thai Embassy in Washington. Apply at the official portal thaievisa.go.th. Passport holders of the 60 countries and territories under the visa exemption scheme do not need a tourist visa for stays of up to 30 days.

faq.question: Can I extend my visa-free stay in Thailand?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says visitors who want to stay longer can, if eligible, apply for an extension through the Thai immigration authorities before their permitted stay ends. Since 15 September 2026 the visa-exempt stay itself is 30 days.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Thailand?
faq.answer: No official source we could read makes travel insurance an entry requirement for tourists. The Royal Thai Embassy in Washington says certain long-stay visas (Non-Immigrant O-A and O-X) require a Foreign Insurance Certificate.
